title: Making and combining promises
description:
Write three functions:

```javascript
function delay(ms, value) { }   // a promise that fulfils with value after ms milliseconds
function promisify(fn) { }      // turns an error-first callback function into one that returns a promise
function settle(promises) { }   // like Promise.allSettled, written yourself
```

- `promisify(fn)` returns a function that passes its arguments to `fn` plus a callback, and rejects with the error or fulfils with the value.
- `settle(promises)` fulfils, once every input has settled, with an array **in input order** of `{ status: "fulfilled", value }` or `{ status: "rejected", reason }`. It never rejects. Inputs that are plain values (not promises) count as fulfilled. An empty list gives `[]`.
hints: `Promise.resolve(p)` turns a plain value into a promise and leaves a promise as it is; `then(onFulfilled, onRejected)` maps both outcomes to objects.
`Promise.all` over the mapped promises never rejects, because every one of them has already handled its rejection.
